`readagau` is designed to make network retrieval explicit and parsing
replayable. This article uses package-owned synthetic fixtures and a temporary
cache, so its executable path is offline and does not write to a home
directory. A guarded live example appears at the end for maintainers who
choose to opt in deliberately.

## Start with a managed, writable cache

The default `agau_cache_dir()` uses `tools::R_user_dir("readagau", "cache")`.
It is separate from the project working tree. For tests, vignettes, and
reproducible pipelines, an explicit temporary or project cache is easier to
inspect and clean:

```{r offline-setup}
library(readagau)
library(knitr)

cache_dir <- tempfile("readagau-troubleshooting-cache-", tmpdir = tempdir())
dir.create(cache_dir, recursive = TRUE)
fixture <- system.file(
  "fixtures", "workbooks", "crop-state.xlsx", package = "readagau"
)
stopifnot(nzchar(fixture), file.exists(fixture))

offline <- read_crop_report(
  c(state = fixture),
  assets = "state",
  view = "reported",
  cache_dir = cache_dir
)

kable(data.frame(
  rows = nrow(offline),
  identity = unique(offline$release_id),
  release_date = as.character(unique(offline$release_date)),
  cache_is_writable = file.access(cache_dir, 2L) == 0L,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
), row.names = FALSE)
```

Local paths are parsed without network access. Because no official release
metadata was supplied, the identity is checksum-qualified and the date is
`NA`. Use `release_id` and `release_date` together only after matching a
local file to a reviewed release. Never put credentials in a source URL or
commit a credential-bearing cache.

## What is cached and how replay works

Raw bytes are promoted atomically to
`raw/<product>/<release_id>/<sha256>/<asset>`. The corresponding manifest
records the exact URL, source filename, byte format, retrieval headers, size,
hash, local path, and validation status. Parsed observations are cached under a
separate key that includes the source hash and parser profile. `refresh = TRUE`
may discover a new page or byte sequence, but it does not overwrite an older
hash-addressed object; `refresh = FALSE` reuses a valid exact cache entry.

The cache writer below is internal only because it lets this vignette seed a
cache from a packaged fixture. The public `download_agau_release()` call then
replays the exact asset without contacting the source:

```{r cache-replay}
release_id <- "acr-2026-06-02-no-218"
manifest <- readagau:::agau_cache_asset(
  product = "crop_report",
  release_id = release_id,
  asset_type = "state",
  source_url = fixture,
  cache_dir = cache_dir
)
replayed <- download_agau_release(
  product = "crop_report",
  release = release_id,
  assets = "state",
  cache_dir = cache_dir
)

kable(data.frame(
  raw_path_contains_hash = identical(
    manifest$sha256, basename(dirname(manifest$local_path))
  ),
  replay_same_sha256 = identical(manifest$sha256, replayed$sha256[[1]]),
  replay_detected_format = replayed$detected_format[[1]],
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
), row.names = FALSE)
```

This is also why a cache directory should be backed up as evidence, not
treated as a mutable download folder. Keep the manifest and the source hash
with any published result. Automatic pruning is not performed by the package.

## Offline, network, and credentials

Use one of these approaches when a job must be reproducible or run without a
network:

* pass a local HTML, text, PDF, Word, or workbook path to the relevant reader;
* resolve an exact release once, retain its manifest and raw bytes, and replay
  it with `refresh = FALSE`; or
* use the small packaged fixtures in tests and vignettes.

The `latest` selector and `refresh = TRUE` are intentionally online-capable
operations. They should be kept out of ordinary test code and out of CRAN
examples. Network retrieval uses HTTPS, bounded request timeouts, and retries;
an unavailable endpoint is reported as a typed package condition rather than
silently returning a partial table.

## Typed conditions are actionable

Errors and warnings inherit from `condition` and carry a stable `agau_*`
subclass plus contextual fields such as `product`, `release_id`,
`asset_type`, and `remediation`. Catch the specific subclass when a
workflow needs a recovery path:

```{r typed-condition}
missing_path <- file.path(cache_dir, "does-not-exist.xlsx")
missing_condition <- tryCatch(
  agau_detect_format(missing_path),
  agau_asset_missing_error = function(e) e
)

bad_path <- file.path(cache_dir, "html-disguised-as-workbook.xlsx")
writeLines(c(
  "<!doctype html>",
  "<html><body>Synthetic error fixture</body></html>"
), bad_path)
format_condition <- tryCatch(
  read_crop_report(
    c(national = bad_path),
    assets = "national",
    cache_dir = cache_dir
  ),
  agau_asset_format_error = function(e) e
)

kable(data.frame(
  class = c(class(missing_condition)[1L], class(format_condition)[1L]),
  message = c(
    conditionMessage(missing_condition),
    conditionMessage(format_condition)
  ),
  remediation = c(
    missing_condition$remediation,
    format_condition$remediation
  ),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
), row.names = FALSE)
```

The main condition families are:

* `agau_release_discovery_error` for missing or ambiguous release metadata;
* `agau_asset_missing_error` for absent or unsupported exact assets;
* `agau_download_error` for retrieval or atomic-promotion failures;
* `agau_asset_format_error` for bytes that do not match the requested role;
* `agau_schema_error` and `agau_table_parse_error` for changed structure or
  incomplete parsing;
* `agau_dependency_error` for a required local executable such as Poppler;
* `agau_endpoint_error` for source endpoints that cannot satisfy their
  documented contract;
* `agau_validation_error` for invalid semantic joins, cache state, or input
  contracts; and
* `agau_status_warning`, `agau_duplicate_warning`, and
  `agau_cadence_warning` for non-fatal source-quality signals.

Do not catch a broad `error` and continue with unlabelled data. Preserve the
condition's message and remediation in logs, and inspect the raw hash before
retrying.

## Troubleshooting by failure mode

### Network or changed landing page

Use a local snapshot or an exact cached release to separate network problems
from parser problems. If a live request fails, retry with the same exact ID and
`refresh = FALSE` first. If the page or asset has changed, retain the old hash,
then opt into `refresh = TRUE` and compare the new manifest. Avoid constructing
URLs from filenames: release pages and asset links are discovered metadata.

### Cache permissions and temporary files

The cache directory must be writable by the current R process. Check it without
changing permissions or deleting anything:

```{r cache-permissions}
kable(data.frame(
  cache_dir = cache_dir,
  exists = dir.exists(cache_dir),
  writable = file.access(cache_dir, 2L) == 0L,
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
), row.names = FALSE)
```

On a write, lock, staging, or atomic-rename failure, check free space,
permissions, and whether another process has left a stale lock. The package
uses `tempdir()` for transient downloads and staged writes; do not redirect it
to a home or global workspace. Cache write failures are surfaced as
`agau_download_error` or `agau_validation_error` with remediation text.

### Poppler and PDF layout

PDF-backed Weekly history requires the `pdftotext` executable from Poppler;
workbook readers do not. Check availability before selecting a PDF path:

```{r poppler-check}
pdftotext <- Sys.which("pdftotext")
kable(data.frame(
  executable = "pdftotext",
  available = nzchar(pdftotext),
  path = if (nzchar(pdftotext)) pdftotext else "not on PATH",
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
), row.names = FALSE)
```

If Poppler is absent, the PDF path reports `agau_dependency_error` with an
installation remediation. If Poppler is present but text extraction fails,
the parser reports `agau_table_parse_error`; retain the PDF hash and inspect
the extracted text rather than silently substituting values. PDF parsing uses
layout-preserving extraction because column spacing, headers, missing-value
tokens, and report-era profiles are part of the parser contract.

### HTML layout, chart descriptions, and schema drift

HTML readers expect the documented table columns and, for current Weekly chart
pages, dated accessible `alt` text. A publisher redesign can therefore cause
`agau_schema_error` or `agau_table_parse_error` even when the page still opens
in a browser. Save the exact page bytes, inspect its `sha256`, and report the
release ID and asset role. Do not patch values in a cached file: a new byte
sequence must get a new hash-addressed entry.

## Optional live smoke test

The following code is deliberately opt-in. It is not run during ordinary
vignette builds or package checks; set `READAGAU_RUN_LIVE=true` only when network
access is expected and the result is disposable:

```{r live-smoke, results = 'asis'}
if (interactive() && identical(Sys.getenv("READAGAU_RUN_LIVE"), "true")) {
  live_cache <- tempfile("readagau-live-cache-", tmpdir = tempdir())
  dir.create(live_cache, recursive = TRUE)
  live <- list_agau_releases(
    products = "crop_report",
    refresh = TRUE,
    cache_dir = live_cache
  )
  print(utils::head(live[, c("release_id", "release_date", "asset_status")]))
} else {
  cat("Live smoke test skipped; run interactively with READAGAU_RUN_LIVE=true to opt in.\\n")
}
```
